case_title: Northern Mineral Ltd. v. Union of India and Anr.
statutory_provisions: Insecticides Act, 1968 s.29; s.24(3) and s.24(4) (evidentiary provisions)
evidence_type: Documentary: Insecticide Analyst (laboratory) report; sample and shelf-life details
trial_court_outcome: Discharge application under s.245 CrPC dismissed; no verdict recorded
neutral_facts: An insecticide inspector drew a sample of a monocrotophos insecticide from the shop of the accused's dealer on 10 September 1993. The accused had manufactured this batch in September 1992. The sample was sent to a regional pesticides testing laboratory, whose report dated 13 October 1993 stated that the sample was misbranded because it did not conform to the relevant ISI specifications. A show cause notice dated 1 November 1993 was issued to the accused, which it received on 3 November 1993. The accused replied on 17 November 1993, expressing its intention to adduce evidence in controversion of the laboratory report and contending that the report was of no consequence. The accused did not specifically request re-analysis by the Central Insecticides Laboratory. The Joint Director, Agriculture, gave consent for prosecution on 23 February 1994, and the Insecticide Inspector filed a complaint on 16 March 1994 under section 29 of the Insecticides Act against the accused and the dealer. The insecticide's shelf life had expired in February 1994.
key_evidence_accepted: The Court accepted that the accused had notified its intention to adduce evidence in controversion of the Insecticide Analyst report within 28 days, and that the insecticide's shelf life expired before the complaint was filed. The Court did not decide the merits of the analyst's finding.
post_offence_conduct: Replied to the show cause notice on 17 November 1993 expressing intention to adduce evidence in controversion of the report; no other conduct noted
trial_duration: offence: 10 September 1993 (sample drawn); trial judgment: 13 November 1999; High Court: 5 November 2001; Supreme Court: 7 July 2010
legal_representation: Appellant: Arun Nehra, Shobha, Mohinder Thakur. Respondents: P.K. Dey, Rashmi Malhotra, Rohitash S. Nagar, R.S. Nagar, D.S. Mehra, B.V. Balaram Das
investigation_status: Sample analysed by regional laboratory; show cause notice issued; complaint filed 16 March 1994 under s.29; discharge sought and refused
procedural_irregularity: No step taken by the Insecticide Inspector after the accused's intimation; complaint filed about a month after consent; sample not sent to the Central Insecticides Laboratory before shelf life expired
appeal_history: Trial court (CJM Patiala): discharge refused 13 Nov 1999. High Court: revision dismissed 5 Nov 2001. Supreme Court: appeal allowed; accused discharged
prosecution_argument: Respondents contended that, apart from intimating intention to adduce evidence, no specific request was made for analysis by the Central Insecticides Laboratory, so its non-performance did not defeat the accused's right
defence_argument: Accused argued that notifying intention to adduce evidence implies demand for Central Insecticides Laboratory analysis, that shelf life affects analysis, and that the accused's right was defeated by inaction
legal_principle_applied: Notifying intention to adduce evidence under s.24(3) confers the right to Central Insecticides Laboratory analysis without a specific demand; where this right is defeated by inaction and shelf-life expiry, continuing prosecution is futile and an abuse of process
precedent_relied_upon: State of Haryana v. Unique Farmaid (P) Ltd. (1999) 8 SCC 190; State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd. (1997) SCC (Crl.) 312; Gupta Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan JT 2002 (Suppl.1) SC 516
other_sentence_order: Advisory observation to authorities under the Act to act promptly and adhere to the statutory time-schedule; no formal direction
